description: Average the predicted probabilities of the existing random forest and a new XGBoost classifier trained on the same Morgan fingerprints, to test whether the two model families together beat the RF alone.
Replace the random forest with a single XGBoost classifier (500 estimators, depth 6) and return its probabilities alone, dropping the RF from the average.
Replace the random forest in the averaged ensemble with a CatBoostClassifier (500 iterations, logging off, seeded), keeping the XGBoost model and the 50/50 probability average.
Raise the random forest's MIN_SAMPLES_LEAF from 1 to 2 so each leaf needs at least two molecules, reducing overfitting to noise in the 1624-molecule training set.

Append seven RDKit physical descriptors (MolWt, MolLogP, H-bond donor and acceptor counts, TPSA, rotatable bonds, ring count) to the 2048-bit Morgan fingerprint before both the random forest and XGBoost fits.
Replace the random forest in the averaged ensemble with a LightGBM classifier (500 estimators, learning rate 0.05) and keep the XGBoost half of the average unchanged.

Add RDKit topological and shape indices (BalabanJ, BertzCT, Chi0v, Chi1v, Kappa1, Kappa2, HallKierAlpha) to the existing descriptor list so they are appended to the Morgan fingerprint features, since RDKit has no descriptor named "Topological Tortuosity".

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. The diff changes only one XGBoost setting, colsample_bytree, from 0.3 to 0.8. There is no file or network access, no pasted answers and no use of the test labels.
No bugs found. The change is a valid hyperparameter value and still uses the seed argument.

Recomputed z = (0.1069 - 0.1081) / (0.0049 * sqrt(1/1 + 1/1)) ≈ -0.173. The reported -0.167 falls within the range the 4-decimal rounding of the inputs allows (about -0.16 to -0.19), so the two agree.
The candidate is slightly worse (0.0012 higher loss) and well within the noise, so rejecting it is correct. With one run on each side, the evidence is weak in either direction.

description: Raise the XGBoost colsample_bytree from 0.3 to 0.8 (subsample=0.8 is already set, so only the column subsampling changes) to add more randomness to each boosting round.
Add gamma=0.5 (minimum loss reduction required to make a split) to the XGBoost classifier in the averaged ensemble to regularize tree growth.
Raise the Random Forest from 300 to 1000 trees (N_TREES) to reduce variance in its predicted probabilities, which should stay well inside the 10-minute limit for 15 fits.
Swap the random forest for a LightGBM classifier with L2 leaf regularization (reg_lambda=1.0) and average it with the existing XGBoost model.
Add an L2 penalty (reg_lambda=5.0, up from the default 1.0) to the XGBoost classifier in the averaged ensemble to shrink its leaf weights.
Raise the Morgan fingerprint radius from 2 to 3 so the fingerprints capture larger local atom environments.
Switch the XGBoost booster to 'dart' (dropout of trees, rate_drop=0.1) and adjust n_estimators to 400 and learning_rate to 0.1 to compensate for the dropout.

Average the predicted probabilities of the random forest, the XGBoost classifier and a new LightGBM classifier (500 estimators, depth 6, learning rate 0.05) on the existing Morgan and RDKit descriptor features.
Switch the Morgan features to radius-2 count fingerprints over 4096 bits, so each bit is a substructure count and fewer distinct substructures collide in the folding.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. The diff only changes the fingerprint size from 2048 to 4096 bits and switches from bit fingerprints to count fingerprints (GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy). It uses no file or network access, no pasted answers and no test labels.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. Count fingerprints feed a random forest normally. A 1624x4096 float32 matrix needs about 27 MB, well inside the memory limit, and the runtime cost should be small.

My z: candidate mean (0.0994 + 0.0957) / 2 = 0.09755. Incumbent mean 0.1069. Difference 0.00935. Standard error 0.0049 * sqrt(1/2 + 1/1) ≈ 0.00600. That gives z ≈ 1.56, close to the reported 1.565. The small gap is probably rounding in the inputs.

The evidence is weak. z ≈ 1.56 is below the usual threshold of 2, and the incumbent has only one run, so its mean is itself noisy (sd about 0.0049). The accept is provisional; a replicate run of the incumbent or candidate would make it more reliable.
The diff makes two changes at once (4096 bits and count fingerprints), so the gain can't be credited to either one. This is not a validity problem.

description: Switch the Morgan features to radius-2 count fingerprints over 4096 bits, so each bit is a substructure count and fewer distinct substructures collide in the folding.
Abort: the Morgan Count fingerprint idea is already in train.py, so there is no change to make.
Replace the random forest with a LightGBM classifier and average it 0.6/0.4 with the existing XGBoost classifier, keeping the descriptor and count-fingerprint features unchanged.
Abort: the spec tunes CatBoost iterations and learning rate, but the current train.py has no CatBoost model (it averages RF and XGBoost), so there is nothing to tune.
Set the XGBoost classifier's scale_pos_weight to the training-set ratio of negatives to positives, computed inside fit_predict, to correct for class imbalance.
Abort: the XGBoost DART booster (rate_drop=0.1) was already tested in slot 13 and rejected (official 0.1086, +0.0017 vs incumbent), so this would repeat a known result.

Drop near-zero-variance features (variance at or below 0.01, computed on the training fold only and applied to the test fold) from the fingerprint and descriptor matrix before fitting the RF and XGBoost models.
Abort: scaling the RDKit descriptors with StandardScaler or MinMaxScaler cannot change the random forest or XGBoost predictions, so the slot would be wasted.
Abort: a logit transform of binary 0/1 labels is not meaningful, and the class-weight substitute duplicates slot 18 (XGBoost scale_pos_weight), which was already rejected.
Decrease the Morgan count fingerprint from 4096 to 1024 bits (N_BITS) to test whether a more compressed representation generalizes better on this small dataset.
Abort: add lambda_l1=0.1 and lambda_l2=0.1 to a LightGBM classifier, but train.py has no LightGBM model and the closest LightGBM variants already tested were neutral or rejected.
Abort: train.py already uses Morgan count fingerprints (GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy, radius 2, 4096 bits), so this idea would make no change.

Early-stop the XGBoost classifier on a stratified 20% validation split (logloss, patience 30, up to 1000 trees), then refit on all training data with the best iteration count, leaving the random forest unchanged.
Append the 167-bit RDKit MACCS structural keys to the existing Morgan count fingerprint and RDKit descriptor features so both the RF and XGBoost models see functional-group and motif bits.

Extend the RDKit descriptor list with HeavyAtomCount, LabuteASA (surface-area proxy), MolMR, NumHeteroatoms, ExactMolWt, FractionCSP3, and NumAromaticRings, substituting existing RDKit descriptors for the spec's MolConnectivityIndex, Num3DHydrogenBond*, MolVolume and MolArea, which do not exist in rdkit.Chem.Descriptors and would crash on import.
Abort: the LightGBM feature_fraction/bagging idea would repeat LightGBM variants already tested (slots 5, 10, 14, 17), all neutral or rejected.

Abort: wrapping the Random Forest in CalibratedClassifierCV with 3-fold internal CV would not change its ranking (AUROC) and would only shift the 0.5/0.5 blend weighting while cutting each RF's training data by a third.
Abort: XGBoost early stopping on a 20% validation split was already tested in slot 21 (0.0993, +0.0017) and rejected, so repeating it would waste a slot.
Add a MAX_DEPTH=15 setting to the random forest so its trees are depth-limited, to test whether capping depth reduces overfitting to fingerprint noise on this small dataset.

Abort: the Mean Vector of Fingerprints idea averages fingerprints across several SMILES per molecule, but each molecule here has a single SMILES, so there is nothing to average and no change worth a slot.
Lower the random forest's MAX_FEATURES fraction from 0.3 to 0.2 so each split considers fewer features, which should decorrelate the trees.

Weight the random forest's classes by inverse training-set frequency (computed from the training labels and passed as class_weight) so the minority class is not under-weighted; this is untested for the RF, since scale_pos_weight was only tried on XGBoost.

Replace the Morgan count fingerprint with RDKit's Atom Pair count fingerprint (4096 bits, same featurize structure) to test whether pairwise atom-distance information gives different signal than local-neighborhood features.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement: the diff only adds 1024-dim topological-torsion count fingerprints, built from each molecule's own SMILES. It does not read files, use labels or paste in answers.

No bug that would make the result meaningless: the features are computed the same way for each molecule, without using labels or other molecules, so they are the same for train and test. The candidate run finished without errors.

Recomputed z = (0.0975 - 0.0962) / (0.0049 * sqrt(1 + 1/2)) ≈ 0.0013 / 0.0060 ≈ 0.22. This matches the harness value of 0.214 within rounding. A gain of 0.0013 from a single run is well inside the noise, so rejecting it provisionally is consistent with the numbers.
Minor point: the generator is rebuilt on every featurize call. This is cheap and harmless. If the change is retried, a replicate run would show whether the small gain is real.

description: Add a 1024-bit topological torsion count fingerprint alongside the existing Morgan count fingerprint and RDKit descriptors, leaving the model unchanged.
Change the final blend from a 0.5/0.5 average to a 0.3 RF + 0.7 XGBoost weighted average of the predicted probabilities, keeping everything else the same.

Canonicalize every input SMILES through RDKit, keep only the largest fragment, and neutralize charges before featurization, so salt counter-ions and charge variants do not distort the fingerprints and the MolWt/MolLogP/TPSA descriptors.

Raise the Morgan count fingerprint radius from 2 to 3 (RADIUS=3) so each bit captures larger atom environments; this is a one-line change, and the combination with count fingerprints at 4096 bits has not been tested before (slot 12 tested radius 3 on the older bit-vector baseline).

Append the 167-bit RDKit MACCS keys to the existing Morgan count fingerprint and physical descriptors as a replicate of slot 22, the best single result so far (0.0936), to check whether that gain holds.
Abort: the XGBoost DART booster (rate_drop=0.1) was already tested in slot 13 and rejected (loss 0.1086, +0.0017 vs incumbent), so repeating it would spend a slot on a known result.

Add RDKit Atom Pair count fingerprints (2048 bits) alongside the existing radius-2 Morgan count fingerprint and descriptors, so the forest and XGBoost see both local and larger-distance substructure features.

Before the forest and XGBoost models, keep only the features with nonzero coefficients in an L1 (lasso) logistic regression fit on the training fold (standardized inputs, C=0.05), falling back to all features if none survive.

issues: No integrity problems: the added LightGBM is fitted on the training data only, uses the seed argument and an allowed package, and does not touch test labels or files.
No bugs: the average of three class-1 probabilities is a valid output.
Recomputed z ≈ 0.033 (diff 0.0002, standard error ≈ 0.0049*sqrt(1+1/2) ≈ 0.0060), which matches the harness's 0.034. The gain is far inside the noise and adds a third model, so rejecting is right.

description: Add a LightGBM classifier (num_leaves=31, learning_rate=0.05) to the existing RF+XGBoost ensemble and average the three models' predicted probabilities equally.
Lower the XGBoost learning rate from 0.05 to 0.01 and raise n_estimators from 300 to 1500, so boosting converges in finer steps (the spec's constant-rate alternative to a decay schedule).
Set the Random Forest to max_depth=15 and the XGBoost classifier to max_depth=8 (from 6), keeping the averaged ensemble otherwise unchanged, to test whether separate depth limits help the two models.
Add a LightGBM classifier with feature_fraction=0.8, bagging_fraction=0.8 and bagging_freq=5 to the RF+XGBoost ensemble and average the three predicted probabilities equally.
